blocks.text: Container environment is fixed at creation from image ENV, then --env-file, then -e (highest); `docker run --env-file` parses values literally.

$ docker run -e LOG_LEVEL=debug rag-api        # explicit value
$ docker run -e OPENAI_API_KEY rag-api         # no "=": copy from your shell (unset → not passed)
$ docker run --env-file .env rag-api

items: No quote stripping: `DB_PASSWORD="s3cret"` includes the quotes → auth fails.
`#` is a comment only at line start.
Compose parses .env/env_file differently (quotes, interpolation), so the same file can yield different values.

blocks.text: `docker restart`/`start` keep old values; recreate the container (`docker compose up -d`).

$ docker exec api printenv DATABASE_URL
$ docker inspect -f '{{range .Config.Env}}{{println .}}{{end}}' api

Q: "You changed an env var but the app still sees the old value. Why?" A: "Env is part of the container config at creation; restart or start reuse it. Recreate the container. If it still differs, check the precedence chain (-e over --env-file over image ENV) and the app's own dotenv loader and defaults."

items: docker run env files: no quote stripping.
Env changes need a new container.
